editorial:
Imagine hanging out with two guys who think they are the smartest people in the room, but they are actually just mean. You follow these two business partners who decide to play a sick game. One guy hates women, and the other is just sad over a breakup. Together, they hunt for the most innocent girl they can find just to trick her and break her heart for fun. It feels like you are eavesdropping on a conversation you probably shouldn't be hearing, and it makes you feel uneasy in a way that keeps you glued to the screen.

The acting is super sharp and makes the dialogue feel real, even when the characters are being awful. You will probably find yourself rooting for the girl and hating the guys, which shows how well the movie works. It is a bit slow in some spots, but the shock value makes up for it. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like owning high-quality discs. It is a great pick for a movie night where you want something that sparks a big debate afterward.
endingExplained: The game ends when the innocent girl finds out everything. The men think they have won, but the girl turns the tables on them. She reveals that she is not as naive as they thought. She exposes their cruelty and leaves them feeling empty and pathetic. The movie wraps up by showing that the men didn't actually prove anything except that they are lonely, miserable people who deserve to be alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological dramas and sharp dialogue.
